thread:
maria.g: Heads-up — after yesterday's key-reshard rollout we started seeing KV prefix warmup hit-rate drop on a subset of nodes (~18% absolute drop), plus a couple of OOM spikes on gpu-pool-3. Can infra/runtime take a quick look?
infra-bot: [alert] 2026-02-12T03:12:14Z node=gpu-pool-3 instance=g3-48 mem_pressure=high oom_events=2 tail_lat_p95_ms=320
aj: Which dashboards should we check first? I can pull flamegraphs if you point me to the traces.
maria.g: dashboard -> /dash/runtime/kv-warmup/reshard-2026-02-12 (private). Quick numbers: pre-reshard hit-rate ~83%, post ~65% on the affected hosts. Token latency p95 up ~40ms. OOMs correspond to peaks during bursts of prefetch.
jonah: Are we sure this is just keying? Any kernel selection or batching heuristic changes rolled at the same time?
maria.g: We did a runtime push that landed a tiny batching heuristic tweak (adaptive batch cap) + the reshard. I ran a quick diff — kernel selection stayed the same for those model variants. Flamegraphs (local) show more time in KV lookup code paths and GC-ish spikes on CPU.
sophia: Hypothesis: the reshard changed key distribution and created more small, high-cardinality prefixes that defeat our slab buckets -> fragmentation. Warmup now issues more distinct prefetches, which blows up working set and triggers eviction thrash.
aj: Makes sense. Can we repro locally by replaying traces with the new sharding function? I can run a 1-node replay to confirm.
maria.g: I've got a trace slice (50k reqs) saved at s3://redwood-debug/reshard-replay/193765. Replaying on a staging g4-48 shows the same hit-rate dip and memory churn.
jonah: If that's the case, options: revert reshard, change warmup to be "staggered prefetch with coalescing", or tune eviction/TTL to ramp up more conservatively. Revert is heavy. I'd prefer runtime-level mitigation first.
sophia: Proposed runtime mitigation: 1) Stagger prefetches with jitter and coalescing windows to reduce instantaneous fanout. 2) Increase min TTL for prefetched prefixes from 60s -> 300s for the first 10m of rollout (ramp). 3) Tune slab allocator to bias for many small allocations (reduce fragmentation).
maria.g: Agree. Quick config I tested on one host: ```warmup:
  strategy: staggered_coalesce
  coalesce_window_ms: 50
  jitter_ms: 120
  batch_prefetch_size: 128
  initial_prefetch_ttl_sec: 300
  prefetch_ttl_ramp_minutes: 10
```
aj: Love the staggered_coalesce idea. We should also add a soft cap on concurrent prefetch futures per runtime worker to avoid tail spikes. Something like `max_concurrent_prefetch = 8`.
jonah: Also add telemetry: histogram of prefetch fanout, prefetch concurrency, and per-prefix allocation size. Need those to validate slab change.
sophia: For slab tuning: bump small-slab pool count + enable compact-on-sweep in our allocator for GPU-hosted cache. I can draft a PR with safe defaults. It cut fragmentation in local tests by ~22%.
maria.g: One more angle — kernel selection: even if unchanged, the adaptive batch cap tweak slightly reduced batching opportunity therefore more KV hits per token. If we pair staggered warmup with relaxing the adaptive cap for 5% traffic, we might see better overall cost/latency.
aj: Suggest rollout plan: 1) Patch warmup config + prefetch concurrency limit on 10% of traffic and monitor 24h. 2) If stable, roll to 50% and apply slab config. 3) If still bad, roll reshard back and iterate.
jonah: I'll add the telemetry and a small perf test harness to measure fanout and slab allocation patterns.
infra-bot: Scheduled job: applied warmup config to canary pool (10%): job_id=reshard-mitigation-2026-02-12-01 status=running
sophia: I'll open the allocator PR and link it here. Also adding a checklist for rollout safeguards (OOM guard rails, auto-revert).
maria.g: Thanks team. Please ping here when metrics start coming in. If we see even one OOM after the canary I'm going to pause the reshard rollout. :warning:
aj: I'll watch dashboards and post a summary in 6h. :thumbsup:
jonah: Adding a short-run smoke job: `./bin/replay --slice s3://redwood-debug/reshard-replay/193765 --concurrency 16 --record=telemetry.csv`
maria.g: perfect.
[silence for monitoring]
